//: Declarations of the renderers' Draw namespace that differ between renderers on purpose. Everything else that appears in more than one renderer must be identical once documentation is stripped, and scripts/check-draw-parity.mjs fails when it is not. An entry here that has stopped differing also fails, so the list only shrinks.

allow.Entity: BabylonJS draws a node as an axis triad, so its union admits TransformNode and a list of them. The other two renderers have no node concept to admit.
allow.DrawOptions: BabylonJS has node, simple-shape and material option DTOs that the other two do not, so the union of option shapes is genuinely longer there.
allow.DrawAny: The update slot is the renderer's own object - babylonMesh against group - and those property names are persisted socket keys in saved scripts, so they cannot be unified.
allow.DrawnTag: The carrier a drawn tag keeps its metadata on is an engine convention: metadata in BabylonJS, userData in Three and PlayCanvas.
allow.DrawnTags: The same carrier convention as DrawnTag.
allow.DrawnAny: BabylonJS adds the node arms, because only it resolves a node; and each renderer names its own scene object.
allow.Drawn: BabylonJS maps a node entity to the node it returns. The other two have no node arm to map.
